title: Heat Pump Rebates in Lynn 2026: Up to $8,500 for Oil and Gas Homes
desc: Lynn heat pump rebates for 2026: up to $8,500 whole-home, $1,125 per ton partial-home, up to $16,000 income-based. Lynn still has many oil-heated homes.
lead: About one in six Lynn homes still heats with oil, far more than Boston next door. Those homes get the most from Mass Save's heat pump rebate of up to $8,500. Here is the 2026 math for Lynn.
cards_heading: What heat pump rebates pay in Lynn
cards_intro: We re-read MassCEC's heat pump page on October 3, 2026. Mass Save's own site blocks our checks, so its rebate table comes from a July 16, 2026 snapshot. Lynn is on National Grid's own list of the towns it serves, a Mass Save sponsor.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: $2,650 per ton. The heat pump must be your main heat, and the home needs enough insulation.

cards.title: Partial-home heat pump
cards.note: Up to $8,500, for heat pumps that heat part of the home alongside your old system. Integrated controls are required.

cards.title: Income-based Enhanced Rebates
cards.note: Or no cost, for households that qualify by income. This is not the standard amount.

cards.title: Alternative Energy Certificates
cards.note: A one-time state payment. MassCEC's example is a 2,000 square foot home with a whole-home system.

cards.title: Mass Save HEAT Loan
cards.note: Terms up to 7 years, to spread the rest of the cost.

cards.title: Federal tax credit (25C)
cards.note: Ended for equipment placed in service after December 31, 2025.

after_cards:
Working it out

A 3-ton whole-home system: 3 x $2,650 = $7,950. A 4-ton system would be $10,600 by the math, but the cap is $8,500. The same 3 tons as a partial-home system: 3 x $1,125 = $3,375. MassCEC's cost example for a 2,000 square foot home is $22,000 before incentives and $12,500 after the $8,500 rebate and $1,000 in certificates.
sections:
The US Census Bureau's survey (2020 to 2024) says 17% of Lynn households heat with fuel oil, 57% with utility gas and 22% with electricity. Only Brockton has a bigger oil share among the cities we cover.

An oil home that switches to a heat pump as its main heat gets $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500. If the oil tank is near the end of its life, that is a natural time to switch. If you keep the boiler as backup, the partial-home rate is $1,125 per ton.

Lynn has 37,960 homes. About 48% of households own. Some 35% of homes are single-family detached and 33% are in two- to four-unit buildings. Most are older: 78% were built before 1980 and 46% before 1940. Older homes often need insulation before the whole-home rebate applies, and Mass Save pays 75% to 100% of that.
Does a heat pump keep up in a Lynn winter?
Lynn's average January low is about -4.5°C, and the coldest reading in ten years was -24.4°C. Being on the coast keeps it a little milder than inland cities. Cold-climate models handle that well.
The rules that trip people up

Mass Save's heat pump rebates for 2026 have a few conditions that decide whether you get the big number or a small one. The system must be installed during 2026 by a contractor in Mass Save's Heat Pump Installer Network, and the equipment must be ENERGY STAR Cold Climate rated. Since January 1, 2026, heat pumps that use refrigerant with a global warming rating over 700, including the common R-410A, are off the qualified list. Ask your installer which refrigerant the model uses before you sign.

The whole-home rebate also asks that the home is insulated well enough, and you sign a form saying the heat pump will be your main heat. If you keep your old boiler or furnace running as the main heat, you are in the partial-home tier instead. Mass Save lists a $500 weatherization bonus and a $500 sizing bonus for partial-home systems. You apply after the install, and the deadline for 2026 installs is February 28, 2027.
installers_intro: Ranked by Google reviews (minimum five). We don't take referral fees or paid placements. Ask any installer whether they are in Mass Save's Heat Pump Installer Network before you sign.
claim_heading: How to get a heat pump rebate in Lynn
claim_steps: Book a free Mass Save Home Energy Assessment. It tells you whether your home needs insulation first, which the whole-home rebate asks for.
If your income might qualify, ask about Enhanced Rebates before you get quotes. They can pay up to $16,000 or the full cost.
Get at least two quotes from Heat Pump Installer Network contractors. Ask about tons, refrigerant and whether the system is sized to be your main heat.
Have the system installed in 2026, then apply for the rebate by February 28, 2027.
Claim your Alternative Energy Certificates through the state program, and use the 0% HEAT Loan for what is left if you need it.
faq: How much is the heat pump rebate in Lynn?
Mass Save pays $2,650 per ton for a whole-home system, up to $8,500, or $1,125 per ton for a partial-home system. Households that qualify by income can get up to $16,000 or a no-cost system.
Is it worth switching from oil to a heat pump in Lynn?
Oil homes usually save the most on running costs, and they get the full whole-home rebate if the heat pump becomes the main heat. Ask your installer for a running-cost estimate.
Who is the electric utility in Lynn?
National Grid. Lynn is on National Grid's list of Massachusetts towns.
Is there still a federal tax credit for heat pumps?
No. The federal 25C credit ended for equipment placed in service after December 31, 2025. The Mass Save rebate, the state's Alternative Energy Certificates and the 0% HEAT Loan are still open.
Will Mass Save pay for an R-410A heat pump?
No. Since January 1, 2026, heat pumps using refrigerant with a global warming rating over 700, including R-410A, were removed from Mass Save's qualified list.
How much does a whole-home heat pump cost after rebates?
MassCEC's example is a 2,000 square foot home: about $22,000 before incentives and about $12,500 after the $8,500 Mass Save rebate and $1,000 in certificates. Your quote will differ.
